segments.text: I cloned myself, and it might be the most important thing I've done for my health. There's now a cellular version of Bryan Johnson in a lab that I can use to test new therapies, grow new organs, and develop new treatments. Whoa, whoa, whoa, hold tight. This is not an embryo.

I had a 125 ml blood draw, my cells were extracted, and Yamanaka factors were applied. These are a set of proteins that reset a cell's epigenetic age, restoring it to an embryonic-like state. My cells are now pluripotent. They can become virtually anything. Neurons, retinal cells, kidney tissue, stomach lining. And because they're my cells, my body won't reject them. Now, I know this might sound dystopian to a lot of you, but this is already happening in clinical trials. Parkinson's patients are receiving restored dopamine neurons, and researchers are using this technology for heart repair and eyesight restoration. Friends, this is why

getting an incurable diagnosis is one of the best things that happened to me in a long time. It's opened up an entirely new frontier, and as you've come to expect, I will share everything with you along the way. In a surprise twist, I'm now my own blood boy.
